parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The student places the metre ruler on the pivot. She places a load P on the metre ruler at the
90.0 cm mark. She adjusts the position of the metre ruler on the pivot so that the metre ruler
is as near as possible to being balanced.
The ruler balances with the pivot at the 75.0 cm mark.
Calculate the distance a from the 90.0 cm mark to the pivot.
Record the value of a in the first row of Table 1.1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
She records, in Table 1.1, the distance b from the pivot to the 0.0 cm end of the metre ruler.
She repeats the procedure placing the load P at the 85.0 cm mark, 80.0 cm mark, 75.0 cm
mark and 70.0 cm mark. She records the values of a and b in Table 1.1.
Table 1.1
a/cm b/cm
75.0

Plot a graph of a/ cm (y-axis) against b/ cm (x-axis). Start the y-axis at a = 0.0 cm. Start the x-axis
at a suitable value for the results.
Draw the best-fit line.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the
necessary information.
G = ______

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The weight W of the metre ruler is numerically equal to 2G.
Calculate the weight W of the metre ruler.
W = ______

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Suggest one practical reason why it is difficult to obtain accurate readings for a and b.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Using only the apparatus provided for the experiment, explain briefly how you would determine
the position of the centre of mass of the metre ruler.

A student investigates the time taken for water to evaporate to dryness when heated from above.
Fig. 4.1 shows the set-up. The power of the heater is constant.
• supply of water at room temperature
Plan an experiment to investigate how one factor affects the time taken for the water to evaporate.
You do not need to write about safety precautions.
• explain briefly how you would do the investigation
• state the key variables that you would keep constant
• draw a table, or tables, with column headings, to show how you would display your readings
(you are not required to enter any readings in the table)
• explain how you would use your readings to reach a conclusion.
